item.title: Plato 0.2.0
item.description:
Plato 0.2.0

This is the big one: Plato no longer operates your computer. It used to be able to click and type on your behalf; that entire capability has been removed from the app — not switched off, removed. Plato is now a voice partner: it talks with you, sees the screen you're talking about, and shows you things instead of doing them.

What's new

  • Sign in with ChatGPT. If you already pay for ChatGPT, your subscription now powers Plato directly — no API key needed. An OpenAI API key still works as the alternative, and adding one upgrades transcription and speech to the natural API voices (without one, Plato speaks with the Mac's built-in voice).
  • Voice works out of the box. Hold the push-to-talk key and speak — with no key, transcription happens right on your Mac — and Plato answers out loud with its caption pacing the words.
  • Pointing. Ask "where do I export this?" and Plato's cursor glides to the actual button and highlights it while it explains. Pointing is a gesture — it never clicks.
  • The original look is back. The trailing cursor and its caption bubble return to the classic Plato style.

Why the permission scope shrinks

Earlier versions used the Accessibility permission to read and operate your apps. That's gone. Accessibility now does exactly one small job: when Plato points at something, a single lookup finds the element under that spot so the highlight snaps neatly to it. It is never used to press, type, or control anything. Screen Recording is still how Plato sees what you're looking at while you talk, and the microphone is still just push-to-talk.

Your existing permission grants and stored keys carry over with this update — nothing to re-grant, nothing to re-enter. One more change: Plato is OpenAI-only now. If you had added an Anthropic key, it is no longer used.

item.title: Plato 0.1.0
item.description:
Plato 0.1.0 — first beta

Thanks for testing Plato. This is an early build: an on-screen AI assistant for macOS that can look at your screen and act on your Mac when you ask. Please supervise it and keep it away from anything high-stakes.

First launch

This beta is not notarized by Apple, so macOS warns once when you first open it. This is expected — see INSTALL.md inside the DMG for the exact steps (macOS 15+: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway; macOS 14: right-click → Open).

What you need

  • macOS 14 (Sonoma) or newer.
  • Your own OpenAI and Anthropic API keys — you pay those providers directly. Plato has no backend of its own.

Updates

Plato checks once a day and asks before installing — nothing installs silently. You never re-download by hand after this first install.

Found a bug?

Ping Fahim with what you did, what you expected, and a screenshot.
